overview: Both are hair-like motile structures built from the same 9+2 microtubule arrangement, differing mainly in number, length, and movement pattern.
genZNote: Cilia: tons of tiny oars rowing together. Flagella: one long whip doing all the work.

aspects.label: Number per Cell
aspects.valueA: Present in large numbers, covering the cell surface.
aspects.valueB: Usually one or a few per cell.

aspects.label: Movement Pattern
aspects.valueB: Moves in an undulating, whip-like motion.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Lining of the human respiratory tract (moves mucus); Paramecium.

aspects.label: Internal Structure
aspects.valueA: 9+2 arrangement of microtubules (axoneme), same as flagella.
aspects.valueB: 9+2 arrangement of microtubules (axoneme), identical to cilia.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Both cilia and eukaryotic flagella share the exact same 9+2 microtubule axoneme structure — the difference is purely length and number, not internal architecture.
overlay.memoryTrick: Cilia = many and short. Flagella = few and long.
overlay.commonMisconception: Eukaryotic flagella (like a sperm tail) are structurally nothing like bacterial flagella, which are simple rotating protein filaments, not microtubule-based.
